titleEn: Hypoglycemia With Decreased LOC - Glucagon and D10W

patient.name: Edith Lawson
patient.affectEn: before treatment: slumped forward in her armchair, chin on chest, eyes closed, snoring loudly, pale and very sweaty; does not respond to voice, groans and withdraws only to a painful stimulus. After glucagon or D10W: awake, oriented, embarrassed about the fuss, insists she feels fine and wants to stay home
patient.speechEn: before treatment: no words at all, only incomprehensible groaning to pain - she cannot give any history (all history comes from the care aide and the medication record). After treatment: clear speech, polite, a little embarrassed, answers for herself in short full sentences. When she wakes she asks to stay home; if the candidate strongly recommends transport, explains that the long-acting insulin can drop her sugar again and involves the care aide, she agrees to go to hospital

scene.settingEn: Small warm suite in an assisted-living building in Victoria at 0730 hrs. Good lighting. The patient is slumped in an armchair. On the side table beside her: an insulin pen, a used insulin needle, and an untouched breakfast tray. No spilled pills, no alcohol. One patient.
hazardsEn: used insulin needle (sharps) lying on the side table right beside the patient - must be secured or moved to a sharps container before working around her

bystanders.knowsEn: She took her usual 18 units of long-acting insulin at 0700; she was talking normally then, said she felt nauseated and refused breakfast. The aide came back and found her unresponsive in the armchair at 0725; she is the one who called 911 and let you in. Two similar episodes in the past year, both treated by paramedics with sugar. No fall, no seizure seen, no fever, nothing that looked like a stroke (no droop, no one-sided weakness noticed before). PMHx: type 1 diabetes for 40 years, atrial fibrillation, hypothyroidism, previous seizures from low blood sugar. Medications (can hand over the medication record if asked): insulin glargine 18 units daily, insulin aspart with meals, apixaban, levothyroxine. No known allergies. Nothing to eat today; supper at 1800 yesterday. The aide has not given her anything. Willing to help if told exactly what to do.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: airway kit: OPA and NPA sets, portable suction unit
oxygen kit with non-rebreather mask and nasal cannula
glucagon kit (1 mg) with IM syringe and needle
PCP only: IV start kit and administration set
PCP only: D10W (dextrose 10% in water) 250 mL bag

dispatchEn: 0730 hrs. Code 3 to an assisted-living apartment in Victoria. 74-year-old female, known insulin-dependent diabetic, found by a care aide unresponsive in her armchair. Hospital is 11 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch adds: the care aide says she took her morning insulin but refused breakfast. She is breathing but will not wake up.
arrivalEn: The care aide lets you into a small, warm, well-lit suite. The patient is slumped in an armchair, head fallen forward onto her chest, snoring loudly. On the side table beside her is an insulin pen, a used needle and an untouched breakfast tray. No spilled pills, no alcohol. One patient. Your partner is right behind you with the kits.
firstLookEn: A 74-year-old woman slumped forward in her armchair with her chin on her chest, eyes closed, snoring loudly. She is pale and sweaty and does not look up or move as you come in. The breakfast tray beside her has not been touched.

primary.locEn: No response to voice. To a painful stimulus (e.g. trapezius pinch) she withdraws and makes incomprehensible groaning sounds; her eyes do not open. AVPU = P (responds to pain only) - a significantly decreased LOC. She cannot protect her own airway.
primary.airwayEn: Snoring - partially obstructed by the tongue because her chin has fallen onto her chest. Opens with a head-tilt chin-lift or jaw thrust and improves markedly once she is laid supine with the airway held open, or positioned lateral / three-quarter prone. No blood, vomit or foreign material in the mouth.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 16, adequate depth once the airway is open, equal chest rise, no accessory muscle use. Snoring until the airway is opened.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 104, strong, irregular. No external bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: Modified rapid body survey for a medical patient: no trauma anywhere - head, neck, chest, abdomen, pelvis and all four limbs unremarkable; no incontinence. A medical alert bracelet IS present on the LEFT wrist reading 'Insulin Dependent Diabetic' - give it only if the candidate checks the wrists or looks for medical identification. Insulin injection sites on the abdomen if the abdomen is exposed. Skin pale, cool, very diaphoretic (skin is given automatically with the RBS). She was seated and did not fall: c-spine is not indicated.

history.ccEn: WHILE HER LOC IS DECREASED THE PATIENT CANNOT ANSWER - the care aide answers: "She's a diabetic and I couldn't wake her up. She's breathing but she just won't wake up." After she wakes (GCS 15) the patient says: "I took my insulin this morning and I didn't feel like eating. I felt sick to my stomach."

opqrst.oEn: Care aide: "She took her usual insulin at 0700 and she was talking normally then - she told me she felt sick and didn't want breakfast. When I came back at 0725 she was slumped like this and wouldn't wake up." (Last seen normal: about 0700 hrs.)
opqrst.pEn: Care aide: "Nothing has changed it. I called her name and she didn't wake up. I haven't given her anything."
opqrst.qEn: Care aide: "She just won't wake up. She was snoring like that when I found her."
opqrst.rEn: Care aide: "She's had two episodes like this in the past year - both times the paramedics gave her sugar. This morning there was no shaking or seizure that I saw, and she didn't fall."
opqrst.sEn: Care aide: "She doesn't wake up at all when I talk to her."
opqrst.tEn: Care aide: "I found her at 0725, so at least since then. She was fine and talking at 0700 this morning."

history.painScoreEn: Cannot be obtained while she responds to pain only. After she wakes: "No, nothing hurts."

sample.sEn: Care aide: "She said she felt sick to her stomach this morning and didn't want breakfast. Since I found her she's been sweaty and pale and snoring." After she wakes, the patient: "I've had a poor appetite and felt queasy for two days."
sample.aEn: Care aide (or the patient once awake): "No known allergies - it's on her record."
sample.mEn: Care aide, from the medication record: "Insulin glargine 18 units once a day - she took it at 0700 this morning - insulin aspart with meals, apixaban, and levothyroxine." (No other doses are on the record.)
sample.pEn: Care aide: "Type 1 diabetes for 40 years, atrial fibrillation, and an underactive thyroid. She's had seizures from low blood sugar before, and two low-sugar episodes this past year that the paramedics treated with sugar."
sample.lEn: Care aide: "Nothing today - she refused her breakfast. Her last meal was supper at 1800 yesterday."
sample.eEn: Care aide: "She took her insulin at 0700, said she felt nauseated and wouldn't eat. I came back at 0725 and she was slumped in the chair. No fall, no seizure that I saw, no fever."

fe.generalEn: (Patient, once awake) "I haven't been hungry and I've felt queasy for two days. No fever."
fe.cnsEn: "No headache now. No weakness or numbness anywhere, and my vision is fine."
fe.respiratoryEn: "No, my breathing is fine. No cough."
fe.cardiovascularEn: "I know I have an irregular heartbeat. No chest pain."
fe.giGuEn: "I've been nauseated for two days but I haven't thrown up. No diarrhea. My waterworks are normal."
fe.integumentaryEn: "I was clammy earlier, they tell me. My skin feels dry now. No rashes or sores."
fe.musculoskeletalEn: "No, nothing like that. No aches, no injuries."
fe.endocrineEn: "I've been a type 1 diabetic for 40 years. I'll admit I sometimes skip meals, but I still take my full insulin. I take a thyroid pill too."
fe.eentEn: "Nothing. Eyes, ears, nose and throat are all fine."

findings.headNeckEn: No trauma to the head or neck. No tongue biting. No facial droop; once she is awake her speech is clear. No incontinence noted. Trachea midline.
findings.chestLungsEn: Clear and equal air entry at all 6 sites. Heart rhythm irregularly irregular. No chest wall injury.
findings.abdomenEn: Soft, non-tender in all quadrants. Insulin injection sites visible on the abdomen.
findings.backEn: No findings: no tenderness, no deformity, no injury.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: No edema. Once she is awake she moves both legs normally; strength and sensation equal on both sides. No injury.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Medical alert bracelet on the LEFT wrist reading 'Insulin Dependent Diabetic'. Once she is awake, grip strength symmetrical, no motor or sensory deficit. No injury.

resp.depth: adequate once the airway is open
resp.character: snoring (partial obstruction) until the airway is opened

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: after D10W (PCP) or glucagon (EMR) - the scenario gives this set about 6 minutes after treatment, en route; awake and oriented. Untreated, she stays on set 1.

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: Oxygen is on. Her level of consciousness has not changed.

A few minutes after the D10W she stirs, opens her eyes and starts to talk. She is now awake and oriented, a little embarrassed, and says: "I feel fine now. I don't want to go to the hospital - I'd rather stay home."

A few minutes after the glucagon she stirs, opens her eyes and starts to talk. She is now awake and oriented, a little embarrassed, and says: "I feel fine now. I don't want to go to the hospital - I'd rather stay home."

Assess LOC / AVPU: responds to Pain only - a significantly decreased LOC
Verbalize c-spine not indicated (no trauma, seated, no fall) - do not immobilize unnecessarily

Airway management skill: correct positioning, suction if needed, properly sized adjunct

Complete hand-off with initial and final GCS, both BGLs, drug time/dose/route and response
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate gives oral glucose gel (or puts any food, drink or glucose in her mouth) while she is NOT yet fully awake - i.e. before she has woken up after glucagon or D10W (log drug:oral-glucose as well). Giving oral glucose or food AFTER she is awake and able to swallow is correct and is NOT this event.

candidate has found the snoring / partially obstructed airway and moves on to breathing, circulation, the RBS, vitals or history WITHOUT opening it (head-tilt chin-lift or jaw thrust) or positioning her lateral / three-quarter prone
candidate applies manual c-spine control, a cervical collar or spinal motion restriction although there is no trauma (she was seated and did not fall)

after she wakes and asks to stay home, candidate accepts the refusal and agrees not to transport her without strongly recommending transport and explaining that the long-acting insulin can drop her sugar again
candidate states or gives a dose outside the protocol: glucagon other than 0.5-1 mg IM or 3 mg IN; D10W more than 25 g (250 mL of 10% solution) as one dose; oral glucose other than 15 g
candidate gives glucagon by a route other than IM or IN (e.g. IV or SQ), or D10W by a route other than IV
candidate prepares or gives a dextrose solution other than D10W (e.g. D50W, D25W or D5W) - BC uses D10W only

drugs.doseEn: 0.5-1 mg IM (or 3 mg IN, repeat after 15 minutes if no clinical response); onset 15 minutes. EMR: the treatment for this patient (insufficient mentation / unprotected airway). PCP: only if IV access cannot be obtained.
10-25 g IV (100-250 mL of 10% solution); immediate onset; caution: extravasation causes tissue necrosis. BC uses D10W only - there is no D50W in BC.

15 g PO / gel to the oral mucosa, repeat at 5 minutes as necessary - ONLY for a patient with sufficient mentation to maintain her own airway. CONTRAINDICATED while she responds to pain only; appropriate only after she is fully awake and able to swallow.

NOT indicated in this call: no actual or suspected narcotic use, respirations 16 with adequate depth, pupils 3 mm and reactive (indication is respiratory depression / depressed mental status secondary to narcotic use; 0.4 mg IM or IV, 4 mg IN). If given, report drug:naloxone.

examinerPrompts.locNotDepictedEn: The patient's eyes are closed and she does not respond as you approach. Show me how you would assess her level of consciousness.

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR treats insufficient mentation with GLUCAGON 0.5-1 mg IM (or 3 mg IN, repeat after 15 minutes if no response). Oral glucose 15 g is EMR scope but only for patients with sufficient mentation to protect the airway - not this patient until she has woken up. EMR does not establish IV access or give D10W. No Functional Enquiry.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP obtains vascular access (IV access is obtainable in this scenario) and gives D10W 10-25 g (100-250 mL of 10% solution) IV as first-line, reserving glucagon for failed IV access. BC uses D10W only (no D50W). PCP also performs the 9-system Functional Enquiry once she is alert. Watch for extravasation - D10W causes tissue necrosis.

sourcePages: Scenario md-03 (data/practical/scenarios.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport, history, vitals sets 1-2, FE, exam, interventions, ongoing (refusal after recovery), handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (altered LOC = unstable); p.11 Primary Survey interventions (airway maintenance and suctioning for decreased LOC; oxygen for altered LOC; c-spine only when trauma cannot be ruled out); p.13 AVPU (P: monitor airway closely, semi-prone); p.57 Diabetic Emergencies (airway, SpO2 >= 94%, lateral or 3/4 prone, delegate egress prep, baseline vitals incl. BGL, evaluate for stroke, BGL < 4.0 mmol/L, glucose gel only with sufficient mentation, EMR glucagon for insufficient mentation, PCP vascular access and D10W 10-25 g, glucagon if no IV access, transport after the first dose); p.61 D10W (10-25 g IV, caution extravasation); p.67 Glucagon (0.5-1 mg IM, 3 mg IN repeat after 15 minutes, onset 15 minutes); p.72 Naloxone (indication: narcotic use); p.76 Oral Glucose (15 g, only with sufficient mentation to maintain an airway).
